presenting: Dry cough, low back pain and left heel pain
relevantProblems: Acute exacerbation of chronic asthmatic bronchitis (SCT 442025000)

visitDiagnoses.name: Acute exacerbation of chronic asthmatic bronchitis

scenario: He reports about a week of dry cough that is worse at night, with mild fatigue and mild shortness of breath on exertion
He uses an albuterol inhaler as needed and takes lisinopril, canagliflozin and atorvastatin daily
Mild wheezing was heard on lung exam
He also reports low back pain since about September 24 after lifting, without leg weakness, numbness, or bowel or bladder changes
He reports left heel pain for about three weeks, worst with the first steps in the morning, which began while he was training for a 5K
Plan: continue albuterol as needed, acetaminophen, heat and gentle stretching for the back, heel stretches and supportive footwear for the heel
He was told to return in one to two weeks, or sooner if the cough or breathing worsens, and a referral for therapy will be considered if the back or heel pain does not improve

presenting: Routine follow-up of diabetes, hypertension and coronary artery disease
relevantProblems: History of placement of stent for coronary artery disease (SCT 428375006)
scenario: Routine primary care follow-up; he reports no chest pain, shortness of breath or palpitations since the last visit
He takes his medications as prescribed and tries to walk most days
Foot exam and diabetic eye exam were discussed; he agrees to schedule an eye exam
Blood pressure was reviewed and no medication changes were made

relevantProblems: History of placement of stent for coronary artery disease (SCT 428375006)
scenario: He came in with two hours of chest pressure that began while shoveling snow and eased with rest
One sublingual nitroglycerin tablet given in the department relieved the remaining discomfort
ECG showed no acute ST or T wave changes compared with his prior tracing
Two cardiac enzyme tests were negative
Discharged home with instructions to see cardiology within one week and to return for pain at rest

relevantProblems: Acute exacerbation of chronic asthmatic bronchitis (SCT 442025000)

visitDiagnoses.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with (acute) exacerbation

scenario: He came in with three days of worsening cough, wheezing and yellow sputum, with trouble finishing sentences
He was treated with nebulized albuterol and ipratropium and felt much better
A short course of oral prednisone for five days and an albuterol inhaler were prescribed
Because he has diabetes, he was told that prednisone can raise his blood sugar and to check it daily
Discharged home with primary care follow-up in one week

relevantProblems: Toothache from dental caries of a lower right molar
scenario: He reports a week of pain in a lower right back tooth when chewing and with cold drinks
Exam found a large cavity in the lower right first molar that is tender to tapping, and mild gum inflammation
A periapical X-ray of the tooth was taken and showed decay close to the nerve
Plan is a root canal evaluation, a chlorhexidine rinse for the gums, and a cleaning visit
He was counseled that diabetes raises the risk of gum disease and slows healing, and that good blood sugar control helps
